title: Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Jesus of Nazareth was executed by crucifixion in Jerusalem under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate; Tacitus records the execution under Tiberius. The year is debated, with 30 and 33 CE the usual candidates. Christians understand the event as central to their faith, while the historical core is the Roman execution.

uncertainty.note: Exact year not settled. Astronomical reconstruction by Humphreys (2011), as reported by the cited page, leaves 7 April 30 CE or 3 April 33 CE within Pilate's governorship (c. 26 to c. 37 CE); the page does not state the calendar used for the April dates.

when.display: c. 30 or 33 CE (date debated); Jerusalem, under Pontius Pilate

where.historical_name: Jerusalem, Roman province of Judaea (governed by Pontius Pilate)

importance.justification: Central event of Christianity and one of the best-attested Roman executions of antiquity, with lasting effects on religion, art and law.

audience_note: Concerns an execution by crucifixion; religious accounts are summarized as beliefs, not as established fact.
